newsitem.title: BULGARIA: Bulgaria budget deficit edges down to 72 bln levs.
newsitem.headline: Bulgaria budget deficit edges down to 72 bln levs.

text.p: Bulgaria's central government budget deficit edged down by 600 million levs in the first half of September to 71.8 billion levs or 89 percent of the 1996 deficit target, finance ministry figures show.
Expenditure rose by 19.7 billion levs to 255.0 billion levs in the first half of September, which is 58.1 percent of the year target.
Revenue grew by 20.3 billion levs to 183.2 billion levs or 51.2 percent of the target.
Bulgaria's parliament on July 30 revised the country's 1996 budget in a move to meet higher foreign and domestic debt payments and to keep the structural reform on track.

Revenue was set at 358.2 billion levs and spending at 438.9 billion levs. The deficit was assumed at 4.9 percent of gross domestic product or 80.7 billion levs, up from the original 58.3 billion levs.
Under the revised 1996 budget Bulgaria will allocate 52.6 percent or 231 billion levs of expenditure planned for the year to cover interest payments on foreign and domestic debt.
A new record high central interest rate of 300 percent, in force from Tuesday is expected to put an additional burden on domestic debt payments, experts said.

The government's domestic debt rose to some 600 billion levs at the end of August from 345 billion levs at the beginning of the year and the Finance Ministry has recently started to cover maturity payments on treasury paper issues with fresh government securities.
The central bank on Monday hiked its central interest rate to 300 percent from 108 percent in yet another bid to restore confidence in the falling lev currency. -- Sofia Newsroom, (++359-2) 84561
